summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to INR812 crore and EBITDA rose 37% to INR43 crore, with margin up to 5.3%.
summary.overview: Updater Services delivered 11% revenue growth in Q2 FY27 with EBITDA up 37% and PAT up 62% to INR32 crore, driven by margin recovery in both IFM and BSS. IFM margin improved to 4.2% as large contracts moved past ramp-up and upfront employee costs normalised. BSS margin rose to 7.7% on 11% growth, with Denave's profit more than doubling, while Global (aviation) faced softer traffic and Athena and Matrix showed modest progress. Management declined formal guidance but suggested annualising H1 numbers, flagging headwinds in Denave and Global in H2.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY (vs INR729 crore in Q2 FY26)

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents (incl. MFs and FDs)
financial_highlights.change: As of September 2026; no long-term borrowings

segments.name: IFM
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR560 crore (+11% YoY); EBITDA about INR24 crore at 4.2% margin vs 3.8% in Q2 FY26. H1 revenue INR1,084 crore (+11%); 7 new significant logos in Q2, 13 in H1.

segments.name: BSS (Denave, Athena, Matrix, Avon, Global)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR267 crore (+11% YoY); EBITDA about INR21 crore (+62%), margin 7.7% vs 5.3%. H1 revenue INR520 crore (+9%), EBITDA about INR40 crore (+36.4%), margin about 7.6% vs 6.0%.

segments.name: Denave
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR175 crore (+17% YoY); EBITDA INR10 crore (+110%), margin 5.6% vs 3.2%; PAT INR8.5 crore (+160%). Demand Gen faces ongoing headwinds; field marketing grew steadily.

segments.name: Athena
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR29 crore; EBITDA INR5.5 crore at 19% margin; PAT INR3 crore (+25%). No client losses; two new BFSI clients signed in October.

segments.name: Matrix
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR32 crore (+2%); EBITDA INR4 crore (+31%), margin 12% vs 9.4%; PAT INR2 crore (+14%). EBGC revenue INR14 crore (+15%).

segments.name: Global (aviation / ground handling)
segments.commentary: Softer quarter due to airline capacity cuts and West Asia airspace disruption; no revenue figure given. Management is pushing Global School of Aviation as a less cyclical stream.

segments.name: Avon
segments.commentary: Mailroom and integrated support revenue grew 4% YoY in Q2; a fraud-related issue is partly resolved with some recovery possible.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management suggested doubling H1 figures as an estimate for the full year (H1 EBITDA INR85 crore, PAT INR62 crore, margin 5.4%) and said these margins are sustainable, with headwinds foreseen in Denave and Global.
BSS expected to deliver good full-year results vs last year, though margin percentages may be impacted in H2.
Global expects activity to improve in H2 with festive and winter travel, with steadiness returning around Q4; update due at end of Q3.
Effective tax rate for FY27 expected to stay in a similar range to H1 on a full-year basis.
Labor code PF ceiling change (INR15,000 to INR25,000): full-year impact at worst INR1-2 crore after pass-through, versus INR5-6 crore with no pass-through.
Long term: management expects growth of 11-12% to accelerate; at current rate the business would roughly double in 5-6 years. IFM internal productivity could add 10-15 bps margin YoY.
capex_capacity: Capex plans and capacity utilisation were not discussed in the call.
Acquisition: a target pursued earlier was dropped after valuation talks failed; no active talks now, though another opportunity is under consideration. A deal may not happen this year.
Denave is closing two small step-down subsidiaries, Denave Europe and Denave Korea; management expects no material financial impact.
demand_pricing: India office absorption reached a record 66 million sq ft in the first 9 months of CY2026; GCC leasing about 28 million sq ft in the same period.
White-collar hiring growth moderated to about 2% YoY in September; BPO, ITES and GCC hiring grew about 4%; traditional IT subdued.
IFM: industrial and manufacturing customers together about one-third of IFM revenue; client retention about 95% over a multi-year window.
Global aviation: domestic passenger traffic declined YoY in July and August, with winter schedules cut by most airlines on high ATF prices and West Asia disruption.
Athena: BFSI concentration fell from 85% in FY25 to 80% in FY26; agentic AI deployments now live and billing for two clients.

qa_highlights.question: Expected full-year EBITDA margins for IFM and BSS, and impact of new labour laws?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance. H1 margin 5.4%, EBITDA INR85 crore and PAT INR62 crore; management suggested doubling these as an estimate. Labour code PF ceiling change could cost INR1-2 crore at worst after pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the planned acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Talks fell apart on valuation and the company did not conclude the deal. It is considering another opportunity; a deal may not happen this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR23 crore Avon amount be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: A very small part has been recovered and some amount deposited in court by the accused. Legal and police processes continue. Management has line of sight to some recovery, which would flow back to the P&L, but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: How will Global and Denave grow despite headwinds, and has Global improved in the festive season?
qa_highlights.answer: Global is growing the School of Aviation and seeking more airport business. Management expects steadiness by Q4 and will update after Q3. Denave is pursuing outcome-linked Demand Gen and field marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Effective tax rate for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the full-year effective tax rate to stay in a similar range, with no major swing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate low, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax benefits from 80JJAA for employment creation. Management says the company relies on it less than peers and expects the incentive to continue while employment creation remains a government priority.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term view and growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth of 11-12% should accelerate; at current rates the business doubles in 5-6 years. IFM levers are new logos, wallet share, productivity (10-15 bps margin gain a year) and higher-value MEP and engineering services.

risks_watch: Denave Demand Gen headwinds and uncertainty; management flagged margin pressure in H2.
Global aviation: winter schedule cuts, high ATF prices and West Asia airspace disruption; update due at end of Q3.
Avon fraud recovery is uncertain and legal and police processes are ongoing; timing and amount not given.
Hiring slowdown in traditional IT and BFSI affects Matrix and BSS demand; white-collar hiring moderated to about 2% YoY.
Reliance on 80JJAA tax incentive, which management says will be reduced over time.
Leadership changes: new IFM COO (Rajeev Bhardwaj), Matrix CEO transition from 1 April 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 execution and margin sustainability, but guarded on H2 with explicit headwinds in Denave and Global. Management avoided formal guidance and gave no figures on the Avon recovery or the acquisition timeline.
key_quotes: We don't give forward-looking guidance, formal guidance.
I want to highlight that the margin improvement has come alongside growth and not at the cost of it.
Clients are no longer buying headcount, they are increasingly buying outcomes, productivity and measurable return on their investments.
As we enter H2, we are encouraged by new logo additions in the IFM segment, client ramp-ups in Athena, improving stability in Matrix and steady growth in other businesses.

growth.why: No formal guidance; management suggested doubling H1 (revenue +10% YoY, EBITDA margin 5.4%) as a rough full-year estimate, held IFM 'healthy growth' and 10-15 bps YoY margin improvement, with headwinds flagged in Denave and Global for H2, backed by margin recovery from contracts past ramp-up and normalised employee costs rather than capacity additions.
